shared.text:
# Fieldnote Clinic Pilot: Summary

From 1 September to 15 November, Fieldnote tested its offline notes app in clinics in Pune, Nagpur and Nashik. Nurses recorded 412 patient visits on shared tablets and synced when they returned to clinic Wi-Fi: 168 visits in Pune, 139 in Nagpur and 105 in Nashik.

## Results

The median sync took 38 seconds. In Nashik, where Wi-Fi frequently dropped, the slowest syncs took up to four minutes. No notes were lost, and tablets lasted a full shift at every clinic. Nurses rated the app 4.3 out of 5. The visit template was the most valued feature, reducing visit write-up time from about nine minutes to five. Photo upload was the least liked feature because it felt slow and confusing.

## Incidents and costs

Two incidents occurred, neither causing patient harm. On 22 September, two tablets editing the same offline visit created a duplicate patient record in Nagpur; staff merged it manually that day. On 14 October, an expired sync-server certificate caused a three-hour outage.

The pilot spent ₹18.5 lakh of its ₹22 lakh budget, leaving ₹3.5 lakh for the next phase. Costs were ₹9 lakh for tablets, ₹4 lakh for training, ₹3.5 lakh for support and ₹2 lakh for the sync server.

## Priorities and recommendation

Clinic leads requested simpler photo uploads, a warning when multiple tablets edit the same visit, and printed visit summaries for patients without phones. Nashik also wants to queue syncs until Wi-Fi is stable.

The team recommends expanding to 10 clinics in March, after improving photo upload and adding the edit warning. It also recommends monitoring certificate expiry immediately. A second review is planned for June.
